purpose: Controlled batch actions for the current selected record set, with asynchronous operation feedback.
behaviorProvider: Shared Buttons and DropdownMenus with local async guard.

component: Normalize selectedCount to a nonnegative integer and render nothing at zero. Otherwise expose a named bulk-action region and polite selected-count text.
Guard callbacks synchronously with a ref, then mark local pending state until the returned promise settles. External loading also prevents actions and clearing.
host: Own the actual selected record ids, authorization, batch transaction, conflicts and server persistence.
Return operation promises; keep selectedCount synchronized and decide whether to clear selection after success. Reserve room for fixed-position bars.

Assignment sends owner id or null, status sends a fixed RecordStatus, and summarize invokes its callback. Rejection preserves the bar and displays the caught message or fallback in an alert.
Escape clears selection only when not busy and the event has not already been prevented; it stops propagation. The clear button is also disabled while busy.

Use data-display group tokens for owned presentation, preserve genuine nested component ownership, and verify the same geometry across Fundamental and Fundamental Floating in light/dark. Keep the documented semantics and state model when composing or extending this family.

limitations: This pattern currently targets assignment, fixed record statuses and summarization; it is not a generic bulk-action schema.
No cancellation, partial-success reconciliation or focus restoration after host removal is provided.
Authored source coverage is separate from executed interaction, visual, accessibility and consumer-package evidence.
